meta.methodology: Read framework.md, all reference===100 edges from torahData.js (result: zero), and the full source text torah_100.txt. Scanned the entire source text for explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא, לְשׁוֹן) and for implicit parallel-aspect equalities. Catalogued every concept mentioned in the text and classified the relationship type (bechina vs. eitza) for each.

bechina_language_scan.detail: The word בְּחִינַת does not appear anywhere in the four lines of Torah #100. No equivalent bechina-declaration language (הַיְנוּ, נִקְרָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב used as identity rather than proof) was found. All inter-concept connections in the text are eitza (causal-sequential).

source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: Subject of the teaching — two types are contrasted
source_text_concept_inventory.note: The text speaks of tzaddikim as the topic of inquiry, not as a bechina of anything.

source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: The visible quality that differs between the two types of tzaddik
source_text_concept_inventory.note: Temperament is described as the outcome/product of the Torah-to-deeds ratio, not as a parallel aspect of any other concept. The Rebbe does not say 'mizmag is a bechina of X'; he says Torah boils → therefore the temperament is not at ease.

source_text_concept_inventory.concept: אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה / אוֹר חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה (light of Torah / light of Torah wisdom)
source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: The cause/source: it is from the Torah's light that every tzaddik draws his righteousness
source_text_concept_inventory.note: Torah is the source from which righteousness is drawn — an eitza relationship. The text does not equate Torah light with any other concept via bechina language.

source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: The second variable in the ratio: deeds must match Torah attainment for equilibrium
source_text_concept_inventory.note: Deeds are described in relation to Torah attainment (greater than, equal to) — a quantitative comparison, not a bechina declaration.

source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: Described as drawn from Torah light
source_text_concept_inventory.note: Righteousness comes from (is caused by / drawn from) Torah — eitza, not bechina.

source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: The state that results when Torah and deeds are balanced
source_text_concept_inventory.note: This is the outcome when Torah-to-deeds ratio is balanced — a causal endpoint, not a bechina declaration. The Rebbe uses the phrase 'מִתְיַשְּׁבִים בְּשׁוּבָה וָנַחַת' — they 'settle in stillness and tranquility', meaning this is the result, not a parallel-identity.

source_text_concept_inventory.concept: דַּעְתּוֹ נוֹחָה עִם הַבְּרִיּוֹת (mind at ease with people)
source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: Effect: the balanced tzaddik's temperament is at ease with others
source_text_concept_inventory.note: Eitza outcome of balance. Not a bechina of anything.

source_text_concept_inventory.concept: הָאֵשׁ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה (the holy fire of Torah)
source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: The mechanism by which imbalanced Torah boils within the tzaddik
source_text_concept_inventory.note: The Torah 'boils' its holy fire within the tzaddik whose Torah exceeds his deeds. This is a vivid eitza description — the Torah causes the fire; the fire causes the intemperate appearance. The Rebbe does NOT say 'holy fire is a bechina of Torah' or equate fire to any other concept via parallel-aspect language. It is a metaphor describing causation.

source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: Visible symptom of the imbalanced tzaddik; what outside observers see
source_text_concept_inventory.note: Anger and strictness are the observable effect of the Torah's holy fire boiling within — eitza output, not a bechina identity.

source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: The social other with whom the tzaddik's ease or difficulty is measured
source_text_concept_inventory.note: Background term, not a bechina concept.

source_text_concept_inventory.concept: צוֹרְבָא מֵרַבָּנָן דְּרָתַח (the young scholar who gets angry — Talmudic phrase)
source_text_concept_inventory.role_in_text: Talmudic proof-text (Taanit 4) that validates the teaching
source_text_concept_inventory.note: This is a Talmudic citation used as an authoritative verification of the causal claim, not a bechina declaration. The Rebbe says 'this is what the Sages meant' — but the Sages' statement is itself causal: the scholar is angry BECAUSE the Torah boils within him.

analysis_notes.structural_conclusion: Torah #100 is architecturally a pure eitza teaching. It presents a single two-variable model: [Torah attainment] vs. [Deed level]. When equal: equilibrium → pleasant temperament. When Torah exceeds deeds: imbalance → holy fire boils → difficult temperament. The entire teaching is a causal chain with no bechina nodes. This is consistent with Torah #100's position in the Likutay Moharan canon as a very short, pragmatic, sociologically-observational teaching rather than a mystical or kabbalistic expansion. The absence of bechina language is not a data gap — it reflects the teaching's essential character.
